A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same SAE-SSV study, with readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Material from v1 Appendices A-C is incorporated into the main text of v2; the remaining appendices can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original steering experiments across three language models, cross-dataset evaluations, ablations, feature analyses, and generated examples in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including the model comparisons in Table 1, generalization results in Table 3, ablations in Table 4, and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: The SAE encoding, probe-based dimension selection, sparse steering-vector optimization, and inference procedure are unchanged. Section 3.2 clarifies the computation of the existing language-modeling loss without describing a replacement objective or new component.

E1.justification: Both versions use the synthetic movie-review dataset, TruthGen, and TwinViews-13k for sentiment, truthfulness, and political steering, plus Rotten Tomatoes and TruthfulQA for transfer evaluation. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: CAA, RePe, Top PC, and ITI remain the comparators in Table 1. The unsteered baselines, ablated variants, and methods participating in appendix case comparisons are also unchanged. Baseline descriptions move from v1 Appendix C into Section 4.1.

E3.justification: Models, SAE widths, training budgets, metrics, and judging prompts are retained. The 100 optimization iterations, learning rate 0.05, batch size 64, and inference scaling range 1-10 in v2 already appeared in v1 Appendix B. The intervention-layer list is newly disclosed information, not an established protocol change.

E4.justification: The separability and stability analyses, projection controls, training and LM-loss ablations, feature analyses, case studies, and steering-intensity examples are retained. Matching v1 Appendices D-F to v2 Appendices A-C establishes that these analyses were not added or removed.

E5.justification: The 50-probe ensemble and coefficient-of-variation analysis in Figure 3 are unchanged. Neither version adds evaluation seed counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or a different uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Tables 1-9, plotted results, and appendix output examples are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains LLaMA3.1-8B SAE-SSV success rates of 63.2%, 60.5%, and 34.1% across the three tasks. The new stylistic-transfer statement interprets retained evidence rather than supplying a new experimental comparison.

T1.justification: Equations (1)-(9), feature-selection definitions, and the optimization formulation are retained. No formal assumptions, derivations, propositions, or proofs are added or revised; the LM-loss sentence provides computational clarification.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the central contributions. Section 6 adds the assertion that cross-dataset experiments reveal both semantic directions and stylistic patterns of training data, modestly broadening the conclusion toward a more general steering mechanism.

C2.justification: Section 6 newly interprets transfer as capturing training-data style and motivates style-invariant steering through diverse corpora and objectives that reduce stylistic sensitivity. The existing limitations paragraph is unchanged, and no dedicated style analysis accompanies this interpretation.

D1.justification: v2 adds a public implementation link in the abstract, specifies that the LM loss uses cross-entropy of the positive target conditioned on the steered negative input, and lists intervention layers for every model and task in Section 4.1. Existing hyperparameters and hardware details are relocated from v1 Appendix B.

R1.justification: The bibliography contains the same works. Section 5 consolidates and paraphrases v1's main-text related-work summary and Appendix A, retaining the positioning relative to dense-space steering and SAE-based approaches.

P1.justification: Related work, implementation details, and baseline descriptions move from appendices into their corresponding main sections. Local rewrites, an expanded and retitled conclusion, acknowledgments, and a corresponding-author note are added, while the main narrative and section order remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures, tables, captions, and appendix example displays retain their content and organization. Presentation changes are limited to text reflow, author and footnote formatting, and removal of page-number footers; no scientific display is added or redrawn.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses specific documentation gaps by explaining the LM-loss target, listing intervention layers, and providing code-access information. Consolidating existing details also improves accessibility. The experimental evidence remains unchanged, and the new stylistic-transfer interpretation lacks a dedicated supporting analysis, so the overall gain is limited.
